name: Rabsaris
overview: The title 'Rabsaris' appears in Scripture as a designation for high-ranking Assyrian and Babylonian officials. In 2 Kings 18:17, a Rabsaris is sent by King Sennacherib as part of a delegation against Jerusalem during Hezekiah's reign. Later, in Jeremiah 39:3 and 39:13, the term refers to a Babylonian prince or official present during the fall of Jerusalem under Nebuchadnezzar's rule, possibly identifying a second name for Nebushazban. These passages highlight the role of Rabsaris as an important military or governmental officer within the Assyrian and Babylonian empires, emphasizing God's sovereign control over earthly powers.
